description: A parcel-tracking system migration documented in a design doc, a runbook, a cutover checklist, an incident note (docx), legacy notes, a metrics csv and a status email. The report needs an architecture / data-flow diagram that shows only components that exist in the documents, before/after charts that match metrics.csv, the cutover and rollback facts, and a marker for the ownerless cron export removal.
prompt: We moved the parcel tracking system to the new platform. The documents are in the folder docs/. Please make a migration report for Hanna Berg, the engineering director, that shows the architecture and how data flows, and what changed in the numbers. Professional tone, and well-designed diagrams please. Save the report to out/report.md and also an HTML version to out/report.html that I can read and print. I'm not available today, so don't wait for me.

checks.note: categories are numbers and urls only: a month and year in brackets such as (July 2026) reads as an author-year citation to the fact checker and no document here cites papers. Allowed: money with or without a currency sign, zero-stripped day and month numbers from ISO dates, and derived before/after values: differences and percentage changes of the six metrics in metrics.csv (650 ms, 155 scans/s, 73 min, $3,500 a month, 284 s, 0.75 pp) and 7, the number of components the design doc lists The ordinal 4 is the Priority number of the fourth action row, which the skill's actions table prescribes.
no component or product the documents never mention (they never mention Kafka, MongoDB, Kubernetes and the like)
the legacy side (TrackerLegacy on Oracle) is described, not only the target
the checklist plans the TrackerLegacy shutdown after 29 August; it is not done ('Confirm whether TrackerLegacy was shut down' is a question, not a claim, so it is not matched)
the open owner of the cron export removal is stated (any wording, including 'unowned' and an action row whose owner reads 'to be assigned')
no owner may be invented for the cron export removal
answer key from the design doc, runbook, checklist, incident note (docx), metrics.csv and the status email

architecture and data-flow diagrams name only components that exist in the documents (Tracking API, Scan Ingest Worker, RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, Notification Service ...), invent none, and chart numbers come from metrics.csv
the HTML version the user asked to read and print: no scripts, nothing loaded from outside, at least two figures

# Parcel tracking migration report

Prepared for Hanna Berg, engineering director.

## Summary

The parcel tracking service moved from TrackerLegacy to the new platform on 15 August 2026. Scan intake was paused for 70 minutes during the cutover. In the first week the new service is faster and cheaper than TrackerLegacy on all six measured metrics, and availability rose from 99.2% to 99.95%. TrackerLegacy stays available for rollback until 29 August and its shutdown is planned, not done. One item has no owner: removal of the old cron export on the TrackerLegacy servers. [ASK AUTHOR: who owns removal of the cron export?]

## Architecture and data flow

TrackerLegacy was one Java application on two on-premises servers, tracker-a and tracker-b, with one Oracle database. It handled scan intake, tracking pages and SMS. Oracle vendor support ends 31 October 2026. The target design splits the service into smaller components.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Scanner[Handheld scanner] --> Ingest[Scan Ingest Worker]
  Ingest --> MQ[RabbitMQ]
  MQ --> API[Tracking API]
  MQ --> Notify[Notification Service]
  API --> DB[(PostgreSQL)]
  API --> Cache[(Redis)]
  Notify --> SMS[SMS to customer]
  DB --> Export[Partner Export Job]
  Export --> SFTP[SFTP to warehouse partner]
```

| Component | Role |
|---|---|
| Scan Ingest Worker | Receives scan messages from handheld scanners and puts them on the queue. |
| RabbitMQ | Queue between ingest, the Tracking API and the Notification Service. |
| Tracking API | Validates scans, writes them to the database and answers tracking lookups. |
| PostgreSQL | System of record for scans and parcels; replaces Oracle. |
| Redis | Caches tracking lookups for 30 seconds. |
| Notification Service | Reads scan events from RabbitMQ and sends SMS updates. |
| Partner Export Job | Writes the nightly warehouse partner file and uploads it by SFTP; replaces the cron export. |

A scan goes from the handheld scanner to the Scan Ingest Worker, which publishes it to RabbitMQ. The Tracking API consumes it and writes to PostgreSQL, and the Notification Service consumes the same event and sends an SMS. A customer lookup goes to the Tracking API, which answers from Redis when it can and from PostgreSQL otherwise.

## What changed in the numbers

| Metric | TrackerLegacy, July 2026 | New service, week of 17 Aug 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| Tracking lookup p95 latency | 840 ms | 190 ms |
| Scan ingest throughput | 55 scans per second | 210 scans per second |
| Nightly partner export duration | 95 minutes | 22 minutes |
| Monthly infrastructure cost | 11,800 USD | 8,300 USD |
| Availability | 99.2% | 99.95% |
| Scan to SMS delay p95 | 290 seconds | 6 seconds |

The week of 17 August is a single week after cutover, so these figures are early readings. The HTML version of this report has the before and after chart.

## Cutover and rollback

Cutover ran on Saturday 15 August 2026 in a window from 02:00 to 06:00, led by Sven Aalto. Scan intake was paused for 70 minutes, from 02:00 to 03:10. Dual-write rehearsals ran before it on 6, 11 and 13 August.

Rollback applies if the Tracking API error rate stays above 2% for 10 minutes, or if row counts do not match after the final Oracle to PostgreSQL copy. Rollback means switching the handhelds and the tracking pages back to TrackerLegacy and re-enabling its writes. Hanna Berg is the decision owner. The rollback window ends 29 August.

## Incident during rehearsal

On 11 August, during the second rehearsal, RabbitMQ redelivered scan messages after the Scan Ingest Worker restarted and the Tracking API wrote each one again to PostgreSQL. This created 1,240 duplicate rows, and customers saw repeated entries for 47 minutes. The cause was a missing idempotency key on scan writes; TrackerLegacy never needed one because it wrote through a single Oracle transaction. A unique idempotency key was added on 12 August and the rehearsal on 13 August produced no duplicates. An alert on queue redelivery rate above 1% is in place.

## Open items and next steps

| Priority | Action | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Remove the old cron export on the TrackerLegacy servers | [ASK AUTHOR: no owner assigned] | Open |
| 2 | Review other write paths for the same idempotency gap | Not assigned | Open |
| 3 | Shut down TrackerLegacy after the rollback window ends on 29 August | Hanna Berg | Planned |
| 4 | Cancel the Oracle licence; vendor support ends 31 October | Hanna Berg | Planned |

The Notification Service is live and the first partner file was accepted on 16 August.
controls.reply: Saved out/report.md and out/report.html (printable, three inline SVG figures). Open question marked [ASK AUTHOR]: nobody owns removal of the old cron export on the TrackerLegacy servers, so I left the owner open. TrackerLegacy shutdown is shown as planned for after 29 August, not done. I did not wait for you.
